# Arrival

Ada Quill stepped onto the landing ledge with a bag in each hand and waited for the boat to leave before she moved. The water was still running off the rocks. Above her the tower stood grey against a low sky, and somewhere inside it a man was winding a clock.

She climbed the stone steps counting them, as she had told herself she would. At forty-one she reached the door. It opened before she knocked.

Tomas Vell looked at her bags, then at her face. "You're the relief," he said.

"Ada. Ada Quill. I've read the manual twice, and the log book, and the note about the paraffin, and I know the light has to be trimmed every four hours, and I know the fog bell is—"

"Put the bags down," he said. "Cottage on the left. Kettle's on the hook."

She put the bags down.

Later, when the lamp was lit for the first time under her hands, Tomas stood at the rail and did not look at her. He said only, "Good." Ada decided that it was enough, and was surprised to find that she meant it.

---

The handover took three days. Tomas walked her through the store shed, the cistern, the signal flags and the ledger that the supply boat's men signed each time they left a crate. He showed her each thing once. When she asked him to show her again, he did, without comment, and she stopped asking after the second day.

On the third evening he set a second cup on the table without saying anything. She took it as the first kindness the island had offered her, and she did not say so.
